analysis:
Examined both excerpts and the bounded patch for provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/Inference/Distributed/Installed/DistributedInstalledPairServingGrant.swift. The change to publicTrafficLine (head patch lines 664–678) switches its default declarations to ClusterPublicModels.current and suppresses the speculative-assistant warning when an artifact-scoped assistant declaration exists. Previously the warning applied unconditionally to assistant placements (base lines 664–673, 818–826). This is a changed public-qualification display contract, not evidence by itself of bypassed routing or serving authorization.
The supplied surrounding code scopes qualification decisions to artifact digests (head lines 414–415), ignores inconsistent records (434–435), and removes passing evidence contradicted by a divergence (455–476). Owner serving and public qualification were already separate (base lines 649–658). No changes to encryption, cache scope/storage, credentials, attestation, billing or inference admission are demonstrated in these units; T-041's mitigations are not directly altered here.
Integration must examine ClusterPublicModels.current/tensorAssistant, ClusterConfiguration.validate and coordinator-facing capability/routing changes: confirm a declaration binds the actual assistant artifact and mode, cannot mislabel a different assistant, and does not substitute owner declarations for coordinator parity qualification or current serving authorization. These contracts are outside the supplied source, not observed missing controls. Relevant assumptions include T-007/T-027 (computation/model integrity), T-052/T-053/T-054 (authorization and build binding), and T-056 (qualification must not overclaim correct computation). The patch's final documentation hunk is truncated and the changed head tail is absent; reconcile it and any threat-model implications in the next pass. No independently supported security regression can be concluded from this local scope.
